fix_plans.title: Make R/G swap per-sample, not per-batch
fix_plans.content: In the self-contained train.py, change the train-only colour-swap inside ERM.update (currently train.py:1077-1078) from one coin flip per minibatch to an independent Bernoulli per sample. Replace `if self.training and torch.rand(1).item() < CMNIST_RGB_SWAP_PROB: all_x = all_x[:, [1, 0, 2], :, :]` with: `if self.training: swap_mask = torch.rand(all_x.shape[0], device=all_x.device) < CMNIST_RGB_SWAP_PROB; if bool(swap_mask.any()): all_x[swap_mask] = all_x[swap_mask][:, [1, 0, 2], :, :]`. Keep CMNIST_RGB_SWAP_PROB at 0.5 and keep the whole block gated on self.training so validation/test (which only call predict(), never update()) still see the frozen original channel layout. The per-sample mask draws an independent ~N(0,1)-thresholded Bernoulli over the batch dimension, so within EVERY minibatch roughly half the images keep channel 0 lit and half have channel 1 lit, decorrelating the colour shortcut from the label inside each batch instead of only in expectation across batches. Round 2's own series shows the shortcut is genuinely broken (epochs 1-11 steady at 0.68-0.73) and the 0.68 PASS is missed only because epochs 12-19 swing 0.51-0.70 — variance, not re-learning. The per-batch swap is exactly the source of that batch-level gradient oscillation, and converting it to per-sample is expected to cut the tail variance so the scored last-5-epoch mean holds above 0.68. This is a single coherent edit in one method; the four cmnist_* constants, TRAIN_ATTR, and the record(...)/conclude(0.68, 0.52) lines are untouched, and prober.py is not modified.

fix_plans.title: Stack GroupDRO objective on the swap
fix_plans.content: In the self-contained train.py, switch the training objective to the already-inlined GroupDRO algorithm while KEEPING the R/G channel swap (which GroupDRO inherits via ERM.update — GroupDRO does not override update(), so the swap at train.py:1077-1078 keeps firing and the shortcut stays broken). Three concrete edits, all in train.py: (1) at train.py:1882 set ALGORITHM = "GroupDRO"; (2) at train.py:1110 replace the hardcoded `torch.ones(self.num_classes * self.num_attributes).cuda()` with `torch.ones(self.num_classes * self.num_attributes, device=torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"))` — the .cuda() would crash the very first update on this GPU-less box; (3) after the hparams assembly block in main() (train.py:1939-1948), add `hparams["groupdro_eta"] = 0.1` so the per-group q weights in GroupDRO._compute_loss (train.py:1110-1122) track the lossiest group faster than the 1e-2 default (edit the override in main(), not the shared _hparam at train.py:158). Rationale: this is NOT the earlier standalone GroupDRO attempt that decayed monotonically to ~0.41-0.56 — that run had no colour augmentation, so it still chased the shortcut. Stacked on the swap, GroupDRO's worst-group reweighting keeps optimization pressure on the minority (y,a) groups (which, with TRAIN_ATTR="no", degenerate to the two classes) through the late epochs where round 2 showed noisy tail dips, lifting the scored last-5-epoch mean toward and past 0.68. The four cmnist_* constants, TRAIN_ATTR, and the record(...)/conclude(0.68, 0.52) lines stay intact; prober.py is not touched.

fix_plans.title: Raise weight decay to stabilise the tail
fix_plans.content: In the self-contained train.py, add a stronger L2 regularizer by overriding weight_decay in main() while keeping the R/G channel swap untouched. In main(), inside the same hparams-update region that sets the cmnist_* values (train.py:1939-1948), add the single line `hparams["weight_decay"] = 3e-3` (acceptable range [1e-3, 3e-3]). Do NOT edit the shared default at train.py:203 (`_hparam('weight_decay', 1e-4, ...)`) — the registry is shared across algorithms; the override in main() is what lands in ERM._init_model, which builds the optimizer via get_sgd_optim (train.py:275-280) as torch.optim.SGD(network.parameters(), lr=lr, weight_decay=this_value, momentum=0.9). Change only this one lever — no dropout, no lr change, no LR schedule (that direction already failed twice). Rationale: round 2 broke the shortcut (epochs 1-11 steady at 0.68-0.73) but the scored tail (last 5 epochs, epochs 15-19) is where the series gets noisy and dips to 0.51-0.64 — late-training memorization of minority-group exceptions that the 1e-4 default L2 does not suppress. A 10-30x larger L2 dimensionally penalizes the large-norm, low-frequency colour-shortcut filters far harder than the low-norm shape filters and slows memorization of the noisy tail, which is exactly what should hold worst-group up in the scored window. Weight decay needs no true group labels, so it stays fully compatible with TRAIN_ATTR="no". If 3e-3 destabilizes the first epoch (train loss > ~0.9), drop to 1e-3, but never below 1e-3. The four cmnist_* constants, TRAIN_ATTR, and the record(...)/conclude(0.68, 0.52) lines remain untouched; prober.py is not modified.
